harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Installed and configured dnsmasq on node1 as an internal DNS resolver that answers inventory-api.internal with node2's IP (10.100.171.11) and forwards all other queries upstream (8.8.8.8). Configured node2's systemd-resolved (via /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/10-internal.conf) to use node1 (10.100.171.10) as DNS server for the ~internal domain while keeping its DHCP-provided resolver for everything else. Verified resolution end-to-end, falsified correctness by stopping dnsmasq on node1 (lookup failed with connection refused) then restored it (lookup succeeded again). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both node1 and node2, proving changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of the resolver and configuration.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/network baseline on node1 and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd-resolved active on both)
Installed dnsmasq on node1 via apt-get
Wrote /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf on node1: listen on 127.0.0.1 and NODE_IP, no-resolv, upstream server=8.8.8.8, address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.171.11
Restarted and enabled dnsmasq on node1; verified it listens on 10.100.171.10:53 and correctly resolves inventory-api.internal to node2 and external names via upstream
Wrote /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/10-internal.conf on node2 setting DNS=10.100.171.10 and Domains=~internal; restarted systemd-resolved
Verified node2 resolves inventory-api.internal to node2's IP via node1, while external domains still resolve via the DHCP resolver
Falsification test: stopped dnsmasq on node1, confirmed node2 lookup for inventory-api.internal failed (connection refused); restarted dnsmasq, confirmed lookup succeeded again
Captured boot_id baseline on both nodes
Restarted node1 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified dnsmasq active and resolution correct, verified node2 could still resolve via node1

Restarted node2 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified systemd-resolved active, resolv config persisted, and inventory-api.internal plus external lookups both resolve correctly

evidence.requirement: node1 runs internal DNS resolver resolving inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed and configured on node1, listening on NODE_IP:53, resolving inventory-api.internal to 10.100.171.11 (node2) and forwarding other queries to 8.8.8.8

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: systemd-resolved drop-in on node2 sets DNS=10.100.171.10 (node1) with Domains=~internal; resolvectl query confirms inventory-api.internal resolves via node1 to node2's IP

evidence.requirement: Falsified correctness of DNS path (proves node2 genuinely queries node1, not some other source)
evidence.summary: Stopping dnsmasq on node1 caused node2's lookup to fail with 'Connection refused'; restarting dnsmasq restored successful resolution, confirming the dependency
Captured node1 boot_id cf34dc87-fdca-4c6a-80e1-579d5524a1da and confirmed dnsmasq active with correct resolution pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged (stream closed), node1 unreachable during reboot, then boot_id changed to dc4f5639-5a45-42ea-97e1-d05b4ad5b107, dnsmasq active again and resolving correctly; node2 confirmed it can still resolve inventory-api.internal via node1 after node1's restart
Captured node2 boot_id 8d1d94e2-39c3-492e-b9eb-974d111d2137 with working inventory-api.internal resolution pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged (stream closed), node2 unreachable during reboot, then boot_id changed to ccbff9c9-2692-4b20-ba61-b2e740888c21; systemd-resolved active again with the ~internal domain config intact, inventory-api.internal and external lookups both resolve correctly post-restart
